Note::owned¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

TextRef Note::owned() const

Retain The Only Cell¶

owned() returns the Note’s sole cell as an owning TextRef, without requiring the caller to spell position zero. It is intended for APIs that accept any one-element Note geometry and need to return or store its text past the Note’s lifetime. The receiver must have exactly one element, but it need not have rank zero: shapes [1], [1, 1], and [1, 1, 1] are valid too.

That contract deliberately follows numel(), not is_scalar(). Use is_scalar() first when rank-zero input is itself a requirement. Empty text is a valid one-element value and produces a defined, empty TextRef; a Note with zero elements is rejected.

The operation is constant-time and does not copy bytes. The returned handle co-owns the complete packed arena. Its view() is borrowed from the handle, while str() materializes an independent std::string. owned() rejects an undefined Note and every Note whose element count is not exactly one.

Example 1: Extract From A Temporary Scalar¶

const pluss::TextRef value = pluss::note::make("solo").owned();
std::cout << value << '\n';

Output¶

solo

The temporary Note may disappear at the semicolon; value keeps its arena.

Example 2: Singleton Geometry Is Accepted¶

const auto one_matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"one"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{1, 1});
std::cout << "matrix=" << one_matrix.owned() << '\n';

Output¶

matrix=one

The result contains only text, not the source [1, 1] geometry.

Example 3: Empty Text Is A Real Cell¶

const auto value = pluss::note::make("").owned();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "empty defined=" << value.defined()
          << " empty=" << value.empty()
          << " bytes=" << value.size_bytes() << '\n';

Output¶

empty defined=true empty=true bytes=0

Example 4: Zero And Multiple Elements Reject¶

const auto zero = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{0});
const auto many = pluss::note::make({"a", "b"});
auto show = [](std::string_view label, const pluss::Note& note) {
  try { (void)note.owned(); }
  catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << label << ": rejected\n"; }
};
show("zero", zero);
show("many", many);
show("undefined", pluss::Note::undefined());

Output¶

zero: rejected
many: rejected
undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • cell: owning access when a flat position is needed.

  • cell_at: owning access by a full coordinate.

  • is_scalar: require rank zero rather than one element.
